input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are relatively uncommon and survivable due to strict building codes, advanced safety features, and effective emergency responses. Modern buildings are designed with fire-resistant materials, automatic sprinkler systems, smoke detectors, and compartmentalized floors to contain fires and slow their spread. Regular inspections and maintenance further reduce risks. When fires do occur, alarms alert occupants quickly, and evacuation plans, practiced drills, and clear exit routes help people escape safely. Firefighters are trained to handle high-rise emergencies with specialized equipment like elevators for rescue and high-pressure hoses. These combined efforts make such fires rare and, when they happen, often manageable with minimal casualties.
